text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A group of about 300 disgruntled former liberation fighters (PLAN) protested in Windhoek on Monday at not been given jobs by the government.

- Several European parliamentarians have thrown their weight behind a Himba tribal delegation visiting Europe to drum up support for their opposition to the construction of the Epupa dam in northern Namibia.
- About 100 former PLAN fighters marched on State House to call on government to provide them with jobs.
- A drop in bank and prime interest rates is predicted by South Africa and could spill over to Namibia.
- A demonstration by former fighters clearly showed they are not going to budge in their demands for jobs.

- Charges against 62 members of the Haikom-San tribe, arrested earlier this year for blocking the gate to the Etosha game park during a protest to demand back their ancestral land, were dropped by a magistrate's court.
